title: a reply to a request a bus stop cut short is receipted as given up
intention: A request whose asker was still waiting when the bus process stopped is held as given up by the next bus process at that home, so its late reply is receipted 'bus-asker-gave-up' and does not stand for report_stood to raise; a reply to an id no stop handed over still stands, and an ask older than a day is not carried.
why: Measured 2026-11-11: mail-constrain-stood-600s stood at 10x. It was one envelope, c363a743 (tester -> constrain 'run reply'), re-raised once per bus life. Its request 947d23ec was posted at 16:40:44Z, the second a stale client shut bus pid 427135 down (~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/0/stops.jsonl). The reply came 127 s later, inside constrain's 180 s timeout, and nothing took it: request() waits inside the bus process, the stop ended the wait, and the next bus had no _abandoned entry. A repro (request to the tester on a 20 s proof, bus shut down 5 s in) left reply 05be8bdd standing the same way.
traces_to: Law 7; Law 1; ticket cd2d27fe3261 (bus-asker-gave-up inside one bus life).
how: bus.py: _asked becomes a dict id -> asker, and _ask_since records when each ask was posted. hand_over_asks(path) writes {id: {asker, since}} for _asked and _abandoned within ASK_HORIZON_S (86400). take_over_asks(path) loads those into _abandoned and unlinks the file. server.py: ASKS_FILE = 'asks_in_flight.json'; serve() takes over after land_spill and hands over in the stop's finally after final_flush. Each step is loud on stderr and never stops the bus.

clauses.claim: a bus life that stops with an ask unanswered leaves <home>/asks_in_flight.json naming that ask and its asker
the next bus life at that home serves with the file retired, and the late reply to the ask is receipted bus-asker-gave-up and is not undelivered
in that life a reply to an id no stop handed over stays undelivered
a handed-over ask older than ASK_HORIZON_S is not taken over, and its reply stays undelivered

decisions.text: D1: the hand-over file is JSON {id: {asker, since}} at <home>/asks_in_flight.json, written atomically (tmp + os.replace), and unlinked when there is nothing to hand over. The take-over unlinks it after loading. The proof runs serve() over a scratch table through a driver that replaces serve_forever (as test_every_stop_records_its_cause.py does): life 'ask' posts with _asked=True and returns; life 'answer' posts the late reply and a stray one, flushes, and writes measured.json. Tooth 4 is in-process on BusDevice.scratch.
